anomaly_def.Name: Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Query Plan Selection Anomaly: The optimizer persistently chooses an execution plan that is markedly sub-optimal even though statistics are acceptable.
Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly: The physical devices that host database files are saturated, driving read/write latency and queue depth far above normal levels.
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly: Critical data, log, temp, or backup volumes run out of free space, hitting hard limits that block further allocations.

When all three root causes occur together, the database shows erratic and degrading performance: execution plans that favour full scans or large hash operations collide with a storage layer that is already bandwidth-starved, causing exponential growth in I/O wait time. Simultaneously, space exhaustion events interrupt or abort the very same long-running statements, temp‐space sorts, or log flushes, leading to a mix of plan re-compilations, partial rollbacks, and repeated retries. Administrators observe a chaotic symptom set—frequent plan changes, skyrocketing I/O waits, sudden "out of space" errors, stalled checkpoints, and prolonged lock retention—making it difficult to attribute the slowdown to a single subsystem.

Causally, a poor plan often triggers excessive table or index scans that flood the I/O subsystem, pushing it past its throughput ceiling and lengthening statement duration. The longer run times and heavier spill-to-temp exacerbate space consumption, accelerating volume exhaustion. In turn, space shortages cause failed allocations that invalidate or flush plans, prompting the optimizer to recompile and potentially choose even worse plans, while also forcing the engine to retry I/O on already congested devices. This feedback loop amplifies latency, magnifies log-growth and temp usage, and can culminate in service outages where both performance and capacity limits are simultaneously breached.

entry.official_description: While rebuilding index file %s: Failed to close the index file.
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with file creation, filesystem access, write durability, log persistence, tablespace management, or storage-capacity boundaries.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect filesystem capacity and permissions, verify persistence paths, review log and data placement, and check whether storage latency or write failures are affecting the engine.
